Xeroderma pigmentosum involves a defect in nucleotide excision repair, which primarily fixes DNA damage caused by ultraviolet light — specifically cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers, most commonly thymine dimers.  
Deamination of cytosine, depurination, and single-strand breaks are types of DNA damage, but they are repaired by other pathways (base excision repair, etc.) and are not specifically linked to XP.  

Final answer: (A)
